info.name: ResolveAI API
info.description:
ResolveAI — AI-powered helpdesk and incident triage.

Built in Phase 2 Task 15 from `docs/openapi.yaml`. Import does not produce any of the things that make a collection usable, so those are done by hand here:

- **Login stores its own tokens.** The post-response script on `Auth › Login` writes `accessToken` and `refreshToken` into the active environment. Every other request inherits the token through collection-level bearer auth. Do this once or paste tokens by hand several hundred times over the next six months.
- **`{{idempotencyKey}}` is fresh on every send.** The collection-level pre-request script generates a UUID v4 into it, so the endpoints that require the header never replay a stale key by accident. To *test* replay deliberately, pin the variable in the environment.
- **The Tickets folder chains.** `Create ticket` captures `ticketId`; everything after it uses `{{ticketId}}`, so the folder runs top to bottom with no manual editing.
- **`Smoke Test`** is the eight requests that prove the system works end to end. It becomes the post-deploy check in doc 13 Task 17 and can be run headless with Newman.

Run the whole collection: `newman run ops/postman/ResolveAI.postman_collection.json -e ops/postman/ResolveAI.local.postman_environment.json`

exec: // A fresh Idempotency-Key per send. POST /tickets and POST /incidents/{id}/updates
// require one; replaying a stale key returns the *original* response, which looks
// exactly like a request that silently did nothing.
// To test replay deliberately, set idempotencyKey in the environment — an explicit
// environment value is not overwritten here.
// Applies to every request in the collection.
// Every error in this API is RFC 7807 with a machine-readable errorCode, so a
// failing request should still be a *well-formed* failure. A raw Spring Boot error
// page reaching a client is a bug regardless of the status code, and this catches it.

item.name: Smoke Test
item.description:
Eight requests that prove the system works end to end. Becomes the post-deploy check in doc 13 Task 17.

Headless:

`newman run ops/postman/ResolveAI.postman_collection.json -e ops/postman/ResolveAI.local.postman_environment.json --folder "Smoke Test"`

A non-zero exit means the deploy is not healthy. Every request here asserts something specific — a 200 alone proves very little.

request.description: Actuator sits outside `/api/v1`, so this uses its own `{{healthUrl}}` variable — a `..` segment in the path is sent literally by most clients rather than normalised away. Asserts the app is up **and** that its database and Redis components are, so a green health check cannot hide a dead dependency.

exec: pm.test('db and redis are up, not just the app', function () {

request.description:
**The request that proves the async path actually works**, not just that the HTTP layer does: outbox row written, poller picked it up, worker called the model, result persisted.

Polls up to 20 times at 1s using `postman.setNextRequest`, so a slow provider does not fail the deploy check.
